relations.evidence: If you're using the Query Workbench, you do not need to specify the transaction ID for any statements that form a part of the same transaction within a multi-statement request. notable_absence.finding: No Couchbase Server version, no edition statement, no deprecation statement, and no access-control gate of any kind - confirming the Capella twin record's finding on the Server side too. The syntax section says 'Currently, the only available transaction setting is `ISOLATION LEVEL READ COMMITTED`' - 'Currently' is doing version work without naming a version, which is exactly the pattern the registry cannot represent: an implicit 'as of the version this page documents' claim with no version attached. Reconciliation may want a predicate for this (e.g. currentAsOfDocumentedVersion) or a docs-issue asking for the version to be stated.

cross_component_finding: The Return Value table names nodeUUID ('The UUID of the Query node performing the transaction') alongside txid, which is the observable evidence for n1ql:query-node-affinity: the statement returns the identity of the pinned node. Worth noting because the Capella twin, which cannot offer transactions on load-balanced surfaces precisely because of node pinning, documents the same return value.
cross_product_finding: Three prose divergences from the Capella twin, all on the access-surface axis. (1) Server adds a Query REST API paragraph ('If you're using the Query REST API, you must set the [txid] ... query parameter') that Capella lacks entirely. (2) Server adds a Query Workbench paragraph introducing the multi-statement-request unit; Capella has no Workbench paragraph, because the Capella Query tab cannot run transactions. (3) The reverse direction: Capella's version of the node-affinity sentence adds 'If your cluster uses private endpoints, the load balancer ensures that the same query node carries out all the steps in the transaction' - a deployment-specific reassurance with no Server counterpart, which is arguably in tension with the Capella overview page's claim that the Data API and Query tab cannot enforce single-node execution. Same underlying constraint (n1ql:query-node-affinity), three different consequences documented per surface. The worked-example output format also differs structurally: Server shows _sequence_num/_sequence_query/_sequence_result objects (the multi-statement-request response shape) where Capella shows per-statement cbq> transcripts - a direct artefact of divergence (2), not a cosmetic difference.
version_finding: The only version predicate this page supports is availableSince version:cbq-2-0 on n1ql:automatic-transaction-id, and it is identical on the Capella twin (same footnote, same wording). So the batch's single version gate is a client-tool gate that is deployment-independent. Note the asymmetry this creates: the txid-inference behaviour is version-gated on cbq (2.0+) but ungated and unversioned on the Query Workbench, even though it is the same behaviour on a different surface - if reconciliation promotes implicitlySetsParameter, the cbq edge carries a version constraint the Workbench edge does not, and the registry has no way to attach the version to the edge rather than to a concept. That is a concrete argument for allowing version qualifiers on relations, not only on concepts.
